recs.stt: Ask HN: How do you manage/organize information and knowledge in your life?
recs.x:
Org-mode is a really good replacement for MediaWiki. You can manage links, tables and lists all with simple and reliable text files with .org suffix in Emacs.

 [link]

cites.stt: Grokking Org-mode and putting it in charge
cites.x: I think the main stumbling block is the documentation (as with most things Emacs). There needs to be some use cases or something. Even the enthusiastic bloggers never seen to give concrete examples.
I prefer org-mode[1] on emacs. It's simple, flexible, distraction free and for some reason reminds me of writing on paper. You get the simplicity, while also making it as powerful as you want.

cites.stt: Ask HN: Do you keep a personal journal?
cites.x: Org-mode in spacemacs is my choice, though that is more of a TODO list keeper than writing down personal thoughts. But it is plain text and has timestamps. It is also very flexible and powerful.
An invaluable resource is this Google TechTalk [link] it was my first introduction to org-mode.
